## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

✅ **Gate recommendation: approve.**

The per-model defaults correct generated vector schemas for models whose outputs differ from 768 dimensions while preserving the existing default. The lookup is a small, deterministic solution that avoids an API call during schema construction.

Please mark this PR with the `breaking-change` label: `lancedb.embeddings.JinaEmbeddings.ndims()` now raises `ValueError` for unlisted model names, so callers using those names must handle the new error.

**Documentation:** In the [Jina guide](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/blob/f1c9aef241fea8633efdc2cc3bff9045922f0f1c/docs/web/integrations/embedding/jina.mdx) and the class docstring, describe the model names recognized by `ndims()` and its error for other names; the guide currently directs readers to Jina's broader model catalog.

A table created with 0.41.0 and `jina-embeddings-v5-text-nano` reopens and supports text search on `f1c9aef2`, but appending text fails. With a mocked 768-dimensional Jina response, `Table.add()` receives the vector and then raises `Unknown Jina model` in `ndims()`. The same append works with 0.41.0 and `main`. The stored `Vector(768)` field already specifies the width. [Jina model reference](https://jina.ai/models/jina-embeddings-v5-text-nano/)

Please keep the corrected defaults for known models and allow an existing table to validate generated vectors against its stored width. A dimension option for newly created tables would still leave existing metadata without that option. Please cover reopening the old table, appending a matching vector successfully, and rejecting a mismatched width.

✅ **Gate recommendation: approve.**

The stored-width change addresses the append regression [reported in review](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/pull/4840#pullrequestreview-6084820376), as described in [the author’s update](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/pull/4840#issuecomment-7212888256). Existing fixed-size tables can validate generated embeddings without looking up the model’s dimensions, while incorrect widths still go through `on_bad_vectors`. The per-model defaults continue to correct dimensions when constructing new schemas without a network request.

Please mark this PR with the `breaking-change` label: `lancedb.embeddings.JinaEmbeddings.ndims()` now raises `ValueError` for unlisted model names, so callers using those names for dimension inference must handle the new error.

**Documentation:** Update the [Jina guide](https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb/blob/fc53e889a986f1a20e5421892a2e2030ea9b7adb/docs/web/integrations/embedding/jina.mdx) and class docstring to list the names recognized by `ndims()`, explain its error for other names, and distinguish dimension inference from validation against an existing fixed-size column.

comments.body:
Thanks for catching this. Appending now takes the expected width from the table's fixed-size vector column, and only calls `ndims()` when the column does not record one. The corrected per-model defaults are unchanged.

The new test creates a table with `jina-embeddings-v5-text-nano` (mocked response), reopens it, appends a matching vector, and checks that a mismatched width is rejected by the default `on_bad_vectors` handling. It runs with stored widths of 768 and 512. Creating a new schema from a model with no known dimension still raises the `ValueError`.


This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
